# The board's card editor offers CardModel's fields on a model that lacks them

## Context

The Workstation's planning board (#20884) is the first consumer that brings its own model to `Neo.board`: its work items are timeline events that also carry `status`, `order` and `progress`. A card's editor (double-click, `Enter`, or the card's ⋯ button) on a work item offers these fields, in this order, read from the dialog's labels in headless Chromium on `grace/20884-board-pane` at `914a8f7bfa`:

`Title, Description, Status, Assignees, Tags, Progress, Color, Due date, startDate, endDate, allDay, resourceId`

- Four of them, Assignees, Tags, Color and Due date, are fields the work-item model does not declare. An edit in one is lost without a word: `RecordFactory#setRecordFields` skips a field its model does not declare, so the form takes the input and the save drops it.
- The model's other fields appear under their raw names: `allDay` as a text box holding `false`, `resourceId` as a text box holding a person's key.
- Found while building the fix: a typed `Date` field the user leaves alone reports itself changed. The form holds `2026-11-15`, the record a `Date`, so every save writes the day back as a string, and a time of day would be lost. Only `dueDate` converts its value for the form.

## The Problem

A consumer that follows the family's own advice and brings its model gets a form built for `Neo.board.CardModel`. Nothing in the dialog tells a user which fields belong to the record, and the board offers no way to say which fields its editor should show. The contributor guide #21214 (a board on your own records) will meet the same form.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/board/CardEditor.mjs` `createForm()` builds nine fields whatever the model declares: title, description, status, lane, assignees, tags, progress, color and `dueDate`.
- `ensureModelFields()` adds each other field of the board's model, labelled by its raw name (`labelText: name`): a Number field for number types, a Date field for `Date`, a Text field for the rest, a `Boolean` included.
- `formatFieldValue()` and `parseFieldValue()` special-case `assignees`, `tags`, `progress` and `dueDate` by name.
- The board reaches its editor through `cardEditorModule` and `cardEditorConfig` (`src/board/Container.mjs`, `getCardEditor()`); `save()` routes a status or lane change through `board.moveCard` and anything else through one `record.set`.

Design authority: `Neo.board.CardModel`'s JSDoc: "A consumer may bring its own model: `Neo.board.Container` reads the field names it needs from `statusField`, `orderField` and `laneField`, and the card items name their fields." The editor's own JSDoc: "Adds form fields for any custom model fields not covered by the default set".

## The Fix

In `src/board/CardEditor.mjs`:

1. **The form follows the model it edits.** A standard field is built only when the board's model declares it. The title and status fields are always built, since the board names them. A store without declared fields keeps today's set.
2. **The other model fields read well.** A field outside the standard set is labelled from its name (`startDate` reads "Start date"), a `Boolean` field gets a check box, and every Date field converts its value the way `dueDate` does.
3. **A consumer can name the form.** A `fields` config lists the form's fields in order, as field configs, through the board's existing `cardEditorConfig`. `null`, the default, keeps the derived form of 1 and 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a model without `assignees`, `tags`, `color` or `dueDate`, the editor offers none of them, so no field it offers drops its edit on save.
- [ ] A model field outside the standard set appears under a readable label, and a `Boolean` field as a check box whose save writes a Boolean.
- [ ] A `Date` field the user leaves alone writes nothing on save.
- [ ] `fields` sets the form's fields and their order, and a save writes exactly the changed ones among them.
- [ ] `examples/board/basic` (a `CardModel` store) shows the same form as before, and `test/playwright/e2e/board/BasicNL.spec.mjs` stays green.
- [ ] Unit specs in `test/playwright/unit/board/CardEditor.spec.mjs` cover the first four criteria.

## Out of Scope

- The Workstation's own field list for its work items. #20884 sets it through `fields` once this lands, and waits for it.
- The editor's look in the Workstation.
- An inline editor beyond the card's title.

## Avoided Traps

- **Filtering the standard set by the record's current values.** A field the model declares but a record leaves empty must still be offered.
- **A subclass per consumer.** `createForm()` would be copied whole, and the family's fixes would stop reaching it.
